answer: Each agent identity is assigned one unique data shard to store, like a canyon that holds only its own harbor of cargo. The network issues unpredictable spot-checks, and the agent must return a fragment of its shard within seconds, as brief as a comet flashing past. One machine cannot hold a thousand shards: a Sybil farmer cloning one identity into a thousand faces a thousandfold storage bill, while an honest agent pays for just one shard.
